newsitem.title: USA: High Plains Wheat - Bids mixed, sales very slow.
newsitem.headline: High Plains Wheat - Bids mixed, sales very slow.

text.p: Basis bids for hard red winter in the central and southern U.S. Plains were mixed Tuesday in quiet dealings, merchandisers said.
"With the drop in futures yesterday (Monday), I imagine we'll be quiet this morning," a Kansas dealer said.
KCBT March wheat yesterday settled down 5-1/2 cents at 3.96-1/4 a bushel.

Another Kansas merchandiser noted an increase in farmer selling early Monday, but said that activity dried up as the futures market tumbled. He expected slow sales again Tuesday as farmers decided whether to sell before the end of the year.
"Farmers are asking themselves, do I need the income this year, or should I wait and pay taxes next year," the merchandiser said.
However, he said there is growing concern over U.S. tax regulations and deferred payment pricing. That concern could spur additional sales this year.
Basis values in cents/bu against KCBT wheat, cash=dollars/bu.
(Note: Z=KCBT December wheat futures. H=KCBT March wheat futures. unq- unquoted, na - not applicable)
